definitions.gloss: happiness; gladness; how glad one feels
definitions.explanation: The noun form of {嬉|うれ}しい. It names the gladness felt at a particular good thing, and often its intensity, rather than happiness as a state of life.

examples.japanese: {合格|ごうかく}した{嬉|うれ}しさで{泣|な}いた。
examples.english: I cried from the joy of passing.

examples.japanese: {久|ひさ}しぶりに{会|あ}えた{嬉|うれ}しさは{忘|わす}れられない。
examples.english: I can't forget how glad I was to meet them after so long.

examples.japanese: {初|はじ}めて{自分|じぶん}の{作品|さくひん}をほめられた{嬉|うれ}しさは、{言葉|ことば}では{表|あらわ}せない。
examples.english: The gladness of having my own work praised for the first time cannot be put into words.

notes:
Formed by replacing the final い of {嬉|うれ}しい with さ, the regular way to make a noun of degree from an i-adjective.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {嬉|うれ}しさのあまり: out of sheer joy
- {嬉|うれ}しさがこみ{上|あ}げる: gladness wells up
- {嬉|うれ}しさを{隠|かく}せない: to be unable to hide one's delight
- {嬉|うれ}しさ{半分|はんぶん}: half glad (and half something else)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {喜|よろこ}び: joy — larger and more lasting, and usable of an occasion as well as a feeling
- {楽|たの}しさ: fun, enjoyment — pleasure taken in an activity while it lasts
